data.title: Introduction to the A* Algorithm (2014)
data.author: auraham
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了图搜索算法，特别是A*算法，用于在地图上寻找最短路径。文章比较了广度优先搜索（BFS）、Dijkstra算法和A*算法的不同点：BFS向所有方向探索，Dijkstra考虑移动成本，A*则更倾向于朝单一目标探索。文章解释了这些算法不仅用于路径寻找，还可用于距离地图、连通分量、地图分析等。它强调算法输入的是图（节点和边），输出的是路径（节点和边），但不包含具体移动方式。文章还讨论了如何将游戏地图转化为路径查找图，以及优化节点数量以提高算法效率。最后，文章提供了BFS算法的Python代码示例，并说明如何通过记录“来源”表重建最短路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：A*算法的理解与应用

不同观点：
• **apnorton** 认为A*算法可以视为同一类算法中的一种，通过优先队列的不同优先级来区分不同算法，如广度优先搜索、Dijkstra和A*。这种视角有助于理解A*中启发式估计必须是低估的。
• **leftnode** 表达了对A*算法的深厚感情，分享了自己在大学学习该算法时的经历，并通过手动计算和绘制网格深入理解A*，强调了个人学习过程中的努力和成就。
• **kazinator** 批评了Garmin导航设备在路径规划中的不足，暗示其算法在处理不可达目的地时缺乏判断力，类似于“永不承认不知道”的AI。
• **kriro** 推荐了通过“Romania旅行”问题来学习A*，认为这是一种经典且有效的教学方法。
• **upghost** 提出了对“AI”这一术语演变的困惑，指出AI的定义已经逐渐偏向生成型AI和深度学习子集，导致原有的AI定义变得模糊。
• **deadbabe** 关注在未知环境中实体的路径规划问题，暗示A*在已知环境中的应用较为简单，但在未知环境中需要更复杂的策略。
• **k2xl** 作为游戏开发者，分享了A*在网格益智游戏中的应用，强调了启发式算法在不同类型路径规划中的广泛应用和优化潜力。

补充讨论：
• **ecshafer** 推荐了Red Blob Games博客，认为其在算法解释和伪代码实现方面非常优秀，尤其在构建直觉方面有很大帮助。
• **mysteria** 和 **cryptomic22** 分别通过个人经历和视频分享了对A*算法的怀旧感受和可视化资源。
• **0manrho** 提出了关于A*发音的简单问题，显示出对术语标准化的关注。
• **Kye** 幽默地指出A*不要与天文学上的Sagittarius A*混淆，提供了相关维基百科链接。
• **JohnKemeny** 提到了Hacker News上对A*算法文章的多次讨论，并指出文章标题应包含年份以避免混淆。

争议焦点：
• kazinator对Garmin导航设备算法不足的批评，暗示了实际应用中A*算法需要更智能的处理不可达目的地的问题。
• upghost对“AI”术语演变的困惑，反映了AI定义变化带来的术语使用上的不确定性。

总体来看，讨论涵盖了A*算法的理解、应用、个人学习经历、实际问题中的不足以及相关术语和资源的推荐。

44296523.article_content:
Created 26 May 2014, updated Aug 2014, Feb 2016, Jun 2016, Jun 2020, Jul 2023
Graph search
algorithms let us find the shortest path on a map represented as a graph. Move the blob
(start point) and cross
(end point) to see the shortest path found by the
A* Algorithm
:
A* is one of a family of related graph search algorithms:
Breadth First Search
[1]
explores equally in all directions.
Dijkstra’s Algorithm
[2]
takes into account movement costs.
A*
[3]
explores more towards a single destination.
In addition to finding a shortest path, these algorithms can be used for distance maps, flow field pathfinding, connected components, map analysis, garbage collection algorithms, flow networks, and procedural map generation. There are many optimizations and specializations of these algorithms.
Representing the map
#
The first thing to do when studying an algorithm is to understand the
data
. What is the input? What is the output?
Input:
Graph search algorithms, including A*, take a “graph” as input. A graph is a set of
locations
(“nodes”) and the
connections
(“edges”) between them. Here’s the graph I gave to A*:
Sprites by StarRaven - see footer for link
A* doesn’t see anything else. It only sees the graph. It doesn’t know whether something is indoors or outdoors, or if it’s a room or a doorway, or how big an area is.
It only sees the graph!
It doesn’t know the difference between this map and
this other one
.
Output:
The path found by A* is
made of graph nodes and edges
. The edges are abstract mathematical concepts. A* will tell you to move from one location to another
but it won’t tell you how
. Remember that it doesn’t know anything about rooms or doors; all it sees is the graph. You’ll have to decide whether a graph edge returned by A* means moving from tile to tile or walking in a straight line or opening a door or swimming or running along a curved path.
Tradeoffs:
There are many different ways of turning a game map into a pathfinding graph. Instead of making doorways into nodes, what if we made
doorways into edges
? What if we used
a pathfinding grid
?
The pathfinding graph doesn’t have to be the the same as the original problem being solved. A grid map can use a non-grid pathfinding graph, or vice versa. A* runs fastest with the fewest graph nodes; grids are often easier to work with but result in lots of nodes. This page covers the A* algorithm but not graph design; see
my other page
[4]
for more about graphs. For the explanations on the rest of the page,
I’m going to use grids because it’s easier to visualize the concepts
, but all of these algorithms and sample code work on non-grids too.
Breadth First Search
#
The key idea for all of these algorithms is that we keep track of an expanding ring called the
frontier
. On a grid, this process is sometimes called “flood fill”, but the same technique also works for non-grids.
Start the animation
to see how the frontier expands
→
→
How do we implement this? Repeat these steps until the
frontier
is empty:
Pick and remove
a location
from the
frontier
.
→
Expand
it by looking at its
neighbors
. Skip walls. Any unreached neighbors we add to
both
the
frontier
and the
reached
set
→
.
Let’s see this up close. The tile are numbered in the order we visit them.
Step through to see the expansion process:
It’s only ten lines of (Python) code:
frontier = Queue()
frontier.put(start
)
reached = set()
reached.add(start)
while not frontier.empty():
current = frontier.get()
for next in graph.neighbors(current):
if next not in reached:
frontier.put(next)
reached.add(next)
This loop is the essence of the graph search algorithms on this page, including A*. But how do we find the shortest path? The loop doesn’t actually construct the paths; it only tells us how to visit everything on the map. That’s because Breadth First Search can be used for a lot more than just finding paths; in
this article
I show how it’s used for tower defense, but it can also be used for distance maps, procedural map generation, and lots of other things. Here though we want to use it for finding paths, so let’s modify the loop to keep track of
where we came from
for every location that’s been reached, and rename the
reached
set to a
came_from
table (the keys of the table are the reached set):
frontier = Queue()
frontier.put(start
)
came_from
= dict() # path A->B is stored as came_from[B] == A
came_from
[start] =
None
while not frontier.empty():
current = frontier.get()
for next in graph.neighbors(current):
if next not in
came_from
:
frontier.put(next)
came_from
[next] =
current
Now
came_from
for each location points to the place where we came from. They form a “flow field” and act like “breadcrumbs”. They’re enough to reconstruct the entire path. Move the cross
to see how following the arrows gives you a reverse path back to the start position.
To reconstruct paths:
follow the arrows backwards
from
the goal
to
the start
. A path is a
sequence of edges
, but often it’s easier to store the nodes:
current = goal

data.title: Scrappy - make little apps for you and your friends
data.author: 8organicbits
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了John和Pontus开发的工具Scrappy，旨在让普通人为自己和亲友制作个性化软件应用（Scrapps）。这些应用不必精美，但能满足特定需求，如算术练习、会议成本计时器、参会人数计数器等。Scrappy提供一个无限画布，用户可以通过拖放交互对象并附加简单代码来构建应用，类似于Figma等工具。Scrappy应用是多人在线的，状态持久且同步，用户可在朋友使用时编辑。该项目旨在重新构想软件创作，赋予普通用户表达自我的能力，而无需成为专业程序员。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Scrappy等低代码/无代码工具的评价与讨论，涉及长期使用、移动端支持、开源与闭源解决方案的比较，以及用户对易用性和成本的期望。

不同观点：
• al_borland认为Scrappy的托管性质使其对长期项目不适用，依赖SaaS工具意味着项目需要不断重制。他倾向于使用简单的HTML/CSS/JS或PHP来构建项目，因为这些技术不依赖特定平台且维护成本低。
• RodgerTheGreat推荐了CardStock和Decker作为Scrappy的替代品，它们是开源的并且可以本地运行，解决了对托管服务依赖的问题。
• simonw指出Scrappy在移动端编辑功能的缺失，并认为不应低估移动用户的需求，因为对很多人来说，手机是唯一的计算设备。
• tokioyoyo分享了一个个人项目经历，展示了制作简单应用程序并与朋友分享的成就感，即便没有经济回报。
• selcuka认为"vibe coding"（利用LLM生成代码）不会在短期内取代开发者，但会成为简单系统的重要竞争者，因为LLM已经能够生成相对复杂的应用。
• nilirl认为电子表格仍然是最好的终端用户编程环境，暗示Scrappy等工具在易用性和普及性上仍有不足。
• indyjo对Scrappy的UI设计和编程体验提出批评，认为缺乏代码补全、视觉编程和AI支持等问题影响了使用体验。
• blips对AI生成内容的消费持负面态度，认为这种内容缺乏吸引力，并质疑Scrappy宣传文案的原创性。
• feeley推荐了CodeBoot作为Scrappy的替代方案，强调其无需安装和使用Python创建Web应用的便利性。
• ge96分享了学习Microsoft的Touch Develop的经历，指出封闭环境的学习限制，并转向传统编程语言。
• zupa-hu认为Scrappy的反馈过于苛刻，可能是因为进入市场太晚，未来发展道路会更加艰难。
• Peteragain建议从社区和家庭应用角度出发，考虑类似家族式应用商店的模式，强调无安全限制和邀请制的分享。
• riffraff支持"scriptable components"而非块编程，并指出用户对零成本和易分享的需求是关键因素。
• hiAndrewQuinn展示了利用LLM和简单技术（如GitHub Pages和localStorage）创建实用工具的例子，强调新技术带来的便利。
• p2hari正在开发一个类似的单文件HTML/JS项目，并考虑开源或Freemium模式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Scrappy等工具的长期使用价值、移动端支持的必要性以及开源与闭源解决方案的选择。
• 不同用户对易用性、成本和分享功能的期望影响了他们对工具的选择和评价。
• LLM生成代码的兴起被视为一种重要趋势，可能改变简单系统和终端用户编程的未来发展方向。

44306859.article_content:
UPDATE:
Hello Hacker News!
Here’s an FAQ
for common questions not addressed in the article. We’ll keep updating it and eventually add it at the bottom of this page.
Software is important to people. Most of us spend our workdays in front of computers. We use the computer in our pocket tens if not hundreds of times every day. The apps we use are almost exclusively mass-market, sold on an app-store, made for thousands if not millions of users. Or they are enterprise apps that are custom-built for hundreds of thousands of dollars.
But there isnât really any equivalent of home-made software â apps made lovingly by you for your friends and family. Apps that arenât polished or flashy, but are made to
your
preference
and help you with
your particular needs.
Weâre John and Pontus, and weâve been exploring the potential of home-made software together.
We ended up creating a research prototype that we call
Scrappy
â a tool for making
scrappy apps for just you and your friends.
First and foremost, we aim to contribute a
vision
of what home-made software could be like. We want to make this vision as concrete as we can, by sharing a working tool and examples of apps made in it. Scrappy, in its current state, is a prototype, not a robust tool, but we hope it paints the picture we carry in our heads â of software as something that can be creative, personal, expressive. Made by anyone, for themselves and their loved ones.
What is Scrappy?
It may not be clear what âa scrappy app for you and your friendsâ means. What kind of apps are these? Let us paint a picture with a few examples. (We call them â
Scrapps
â.)
Arithmetic practice for a kid in elementary school.
When outgrown, the Scrapp can be extended with harder problems.
(
try on desktop
)
Attendee counter for a local event.
The counterâs state is shared, so the Scrapp can be used to let people in and out at multiple entrances.
(
try on desktop
)
Meeting cost clock,
to help meetings stay on track. A Scrapp like this can be put together in 15 minutes and shared with coworkers right away.
(
try on desktop
)
Weekly chore tracker.
Let roommates flexibly swap weeks, while making sure to track whose up next, to keep things fair.
(
try on desktop
)
What is it like to make an app in Scrappy?
Scrappy is an infinite canvas of interactive objects. The workflow is similar to an app such as Figma, Miro, or Google Slides â except you can attach behaviors to the objects.
You drag objects out on the canvas â a button, a textfield, a few labels. Select an object, and you can modify its attribute in an inspector panel. Certain objects, like buttons, has attributes like âwhen clickedâ that contain javascript code. When the button is clicked, that code is run â maybe it records the contents of the textfield to a label that acts as a log. You build your app step by step: tweaking and rearranging the objects, and attaching a little bit of code to them.
Thereâs no better way to get a feeling for an authoring environment than to see someone use it in action. In the following videos, Iâm making an attendee counter for an event.
The basics.
I start out by adding a number field to track the number of attendees, and two buttons for recording people entering and exiting the venue.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Reactive formulas.
Next, I add a field for the venueâs capacity, and a warning when too many people have been let in.
I use a reactive formula to control the visibility of the warning and the border color of the field.
Your browser cannot play this video.
A shared, persistent world.
Without any extra work, Scrappy apps are multiplayer.
App state is persisted and synced, like users expect from online documents like Google Sheets or Figma.
Your browser cannot play this video.
The app is always live.
Thereâs no distinction between editing and running. I can edit the app while a friend is using it.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Selective sharing.
I make a variant of the app thatâs limited to only entering and exiting people. This is done by putting a part of the app in a frame, and sharing only that frame. The limited version is still linked to the main app.
Your browser cannot play this video.
Visible, tangible data.
Hereâs what the
Meeting Cost Clock app
shown above looks like when zoomed out, revealing a common pattern in Scrapps.
Outside the shared frame are a bunch of fields used to compute the cost of the meeting. This lets me see the data while Iâm working on the Scrapp, just like in a spreadsheet, which is very helpful for debugging â and it makes future tweaking or remixing easier.

small computing

casual programming

home-cooked software

emancipate end-users

44306859.article_summary: 文章介绍了John和Pontus开发的工具Scrappy，旨在让普通人为自己和亲友制作个性化软件应用（Scrapps）。这些应用不必精美，但能满足特定需求，如算术练习、会议成本计时器、参会人数计数器等。Scrappy提供一个无限画布，用户可以通过拖放交互对象并附加简单代码来构建应用，类似于Figma等工具。Scrappy应用是多人在线的，状态持久且同步，用户可在朋友使用时编辑。该项目旨在重新构想软件创作，赋予普通用户表达自我的能力，而无需成为专业程序员。

data.title: Locally hosting an internet-connected server
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要描述了一个CAPTCHA验证过程。用户被随机选中需完成CAPTCHA验证以确认请求。页面提供登录选项，包括输入账户名和密码，以及"记住我"功能。此外，还有找回密码和使用OpenID登录的替代选项。用户需完成验证才能继续操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何解决ISP在IPv6支持不足的情况下进行网络配置，以及各种工具和方法的比较与选择。

不同观点：
• JdeBP指出，许多北美和西欧的ISP在2025年仍然对IPv6支持不佳，用户不得不采取各种措施绕过这一问题。他提到有些ISP多年未兑现提供IPv6的承诺，用户只能通过复杂的方式自行解决。
• Daviey建议使用Tailscale或Headscale来处理Wireguard和低层网络配置，并通过Caddy或Nginx进行代理。他认为这种方法简化了管理，并且可以轻松扩展设备。
• PeterStuer分享了他使用Pangolin和Hetzner VPS进行Traefic Wireguard隧道设置的经验，认为这种方法简单易用。
• DougN7提出使用动态DNS服务（如dyn.com）来解决静态IP问题，指出许多路由器内置支持该功能。
• KronisLV表示自己选择Tailscale以避免手动管理WireGuard和iptables，并提到SSH隧道不够稳定。
• chazeon担心将IP暴露在互联网上会带来DDoS攻击风险，建议使用Tailscale进行内部使用，并结合Cloudflare进行外部访问。

补充讨论：
• yusina提到拥有静态IP后仍需考虑多方面问题，如电力冗余、IP连接、硬件故障、DDoS攻击和安全补丁应用等，这些问题在本地托管时尤为重要。
• zokier建议使用集中式Wireguard网关，并提到一些自动化脚本和相关工具资源。
• bzmrgonz提出在VPS上安装反向代理并使用Wireguard重定向家庭服务，询问这种方法的可行性和潜在风险。
• anonymousiam分享了20年前使用vtun绕过住宅静态IP限制的经验，并计算了成本节约。
• nurettin表示懒得设置Wireguard，只使用SSH隧道进行连接。
• xiconfjs引用了一个关于ISP成功安装因素的幽默链接。
• politelemon建议使用Cloudflare隧道，无需打开外部端口。
• eqvinox推荐使用VRFs以改进策略路由，认为其更具封装性。
• v5v3提醒在开放服务器前需进行基本的安全设置，并建议在文章中添加免责声明。

争议焦点：
• 使用Tailscale等工具简化管理与手动配置Wireguard和iptables之间的选择。
• 是否应将IP暴露在互联网上，考虑到DDoS攻击的风险。
• 使用动态DNS服务与设置Wireguard等隧道技术的优劣比较。

data.title: Reasoning by Superposition: A Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought
data.author: danielmorozoff
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了连续思维链（Chain of Continuous Thought, CoT）在推理任务中的理论基础，特别是针对有向图可达性问题。作者证明，两层Transformer模型使用连续CoT可以在图的直径步数内解决该问题，而离散CoT则需要更多的解码步骤。连续CoT通过超位置状态同时编码多个搜索前沿，实现了并行广度优先搜索，从而在实际应用中表现更优。实验结果验证了该理论构造与训练过程中的实际解决方案相吻合，且这种多路径探索能力在训练中自然出现，无需显式监督。

Title:
Reasoning by Superposition: A Theoretical Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought
Authors:
Hanlin Zhu
,
Shibo Hao
,
Zhiting Hu

Jiantao Jiao
,
Stuart Russell
,
Yuandong Tian
View a PDF of the paper titled Reasoning by Superposition: A Theoretical Perspective on Chain of Continuous Thought, by Hanlin Zhu and 5 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable performance in many applications, including challenging reasoning problems via chain-of-thoughts (CoTs) techniques that generate ``thinking tokens'' before answering the questions. While existing theoretical works demonstrate that CoTs with discrete tokens boost the capability of LLMs, recent work on continuous CoTs lacks a theoretical understanding of why it outperforms discrete counterparts in various reasoning tasks such as directed graph reachability, a fundamental graph reasoning problem that includes many practical domain applications as special cases. In this paper, we prove that a two-layer transformer with $D$ steps of continuous CoTs can solve the directed graph reachability problem, where $D$ is the diameter of the graph, while the best known result of constant-depth transformers with discrete CoTs requires $O(n^2)$ decoding steps where $n$ is the number of vertices ($D<n$). In our construction, each continuous thought vector is a superposition state that encodes multiple search frontiers simultaneously (i.e., parallel breadth-first search (BFS)), while discrete CoTs must choose a single path sampled from the superposition state, which leads to sequential search that requires many more steps and may be trapped into local solutions. We also performed extensive experiments to verify that our theoretical construction aligns well with the empirical solution obtained via training dynamics. Notably, encoding of multiple search frontiers as a superposition state automatically emerges in training continuous CoTs, without explicit supervision to guide the model to explore multiple paths simultaneously.

Real-Time Action Chunking with Large Models
Published
June 9, 2025
Email
research@physicalintelligence.company
Kevin Black, Manuel Y. Galliker, Sergey Levine
Paper
Unlike chatbots or image generators, robots must operate in
real time
. While a robot is “thinking”, the world around it
evolves according to physical laws, so delays between inputs and outputs have a tangible impact on performance. For a
language model, the difference between fast and slow generation is a satisfied or annoyed user; for a
vision-language-action model (VLA), it could be the difference between a robot handing you a hot coffee or spilling it in
your lap. While VLAs have achieved
promising results
in open-world
generalization, they can be slow to run. Like their cousins in language and vision, these models have billions of
parameters and require heavy-duty GPUs. On edge devices like mobile robots, that adds even more latency for network
communication between a centralized inference server and the robot
1
.
To build a
real-time system
with VLAs, we are going to need some form of asynchrony: that is, we must let a model think
about its future actions while executing a previous one.
Action chunking
— where a robot outputs and executes a
sequence of multiple actions for each inference call — provides a good starting point.
Our
VLAs
all use a chunk size of 50 actions, corresponding to 1 second of real time.
However, chunking alone is not enough. When we switch chunks, the new actions might not “agree” with the old ones,
causing discontinuities and unsafe accelerations. Trying to naively smooth over these discontinuities is not guaranteed
to produce valid actions, and can have disastrous consequences.
The aforementioned disastrous consequences. These results are obtained by
attempting to do real-time inference with temporal ensembling to smooth over the discontinuities, a popular prior method
introduced in
ACT
(Zhou et al., 2023).
As a result, in
π
0
,
π
0
-FAST, and
π
0.5
, we did not use a real-time strategy
2
. We executed actions
synchronously
,
meaning that we would finish executing one chunk, wait for model inference, and then begin executing the next one. This
way, the robot started each chunk from rest, and we circumvented the issues that arise from switching chunks
while in motion. However, this introduces pauses between chunks that are still harmful — these pauses aren't in
the training data. Not to mention: they slow things down, are ugly to look at, and discourage us from scaling up the size
of our models.
To solve these problems, we developed an algorithm that we call
real-time chunking
(RTC)
. It enables real-time
execution without discontinuities, and it works on any diffusion- or flow-based VLA — including
π
0.5
— with
no
training-time changes
. We found that RTC significantly sped up execution time for all the tasks we tested. It was also
very robust to latency, even when we injected artificial delays to cause much higher latencies than normal. RTC
completed dynamic and precise tasks, like striking a match or plugging in an Ethernet cable, with inference delays of
more than 300 milliseconds.
Thinking while moving
replay
Action chunk 1
Action chunk 2
When there is an inference delay, real-time execution requires careful consideration. While a new chunk is generated
(red), the previous chunk (green) continues executing. If the new chunk is substantially different — which it often is —
switching to the new chunk results in disaster.
The core challenge of real-time execution is to maintain consistency between action chunks. By the time a new chunk has
been generated by the model, the previous one has already been executed partway. Without a specialized algorithm, the new
chunk might be totally incompatible with the robot's current trajectory — the model might be reacting to new information,
or it might just be sampling a different “strategy” from its learned distribution of behaviors. Thus, we must somehow
use
the overlapping timesteps where we have access to the remaining actions of the previous chunk. A good real-time
algorithm should produce a new chunk that is
consistent
with these overlapping actions while still preserving the
model's reactivity to new information and ability to make intelligent decisions.
Our key insight is to pose real-time chunking as an inpainting problem. Let's say that our model takes 3 controller
timesteps to produce an action chunk after receiving an observation. The first 3 actions of a new chunk can't be
executed, since those timesteps will have already passed by the time the new chunk is available. Thus, it makes sense to
“freeze” those actions to the values from the previous chunk that we know
will
be executed; our goal is then to fill in
the remainder of the new chunk, much like inpainting a section of an image that has been removed. Depending on the chunk
size and how often we run inference, there will be some number of actions beyond the first 3 that also overlap with the
previous chunk. Ra

data.title: I counted all of the yurts in Mongolia using machine learning
data.author: furkansahin
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者利用机器学习技术统计蒙古国境内所有蒙古包（ger）数量的过程。作者受到一篇关于蒙古帝国历史的播客启发，对当代蒙古社会产生兴趣，尤其是通过Google Maps卫星视图观察到首都乌兰巴托周围遍布蒙古包的现象。由于缺乏现成的统计数据，作者决定自行统计。他编写Python脚本，下载指定区域的卫星图块作为训练数据，并使用开源工具Label Studio手动标注蒙古包位置，以训练机器学习模型。最终，作者通过模型自动识别并统计了全国的蒙古包数量。同时，作者提到计划进一步调查这些蒙古包背后的社会故事。

不同观点：

   - 蒙古包经常建在永久性建筑旁边，以保持与文化的联系。

• **经济与实用性的观点**：
   - [snickerer] 指出蒙古包的经济性和实用性，它们是标准化的，可以在市场上以较低价格购买，并且在蒙古可以随意定居（城外无需支付租金）。选择蒙古包作为住房不仅是出于传统和文化，也是一种理性的选择。

• **技术与方法论的观点**：
   - [shpx] 提到可以使用OpenStreetMap上已经标记的89,259个蒙古包作为输入数据，但可能存在与Google Maps影像对齐的问题。
   - [icameron] 关注模型的误报率问题，例如存储罐、水池等是否会被误认为蒙古包。

   - [sorokod] 询问“预测分数”的含义，如何解读40%以上的预测分数。
   - [unholyguy001] 批评模型缺乏验证和足够大的训练数据集，认为模型可能不准确。
   - [amelius] 对使用的深度学习模型架构感兴趣，并质疑是否有更好的方法解决这个问题。
   - [xenophonf] 强调机器学习算法的随机性和不确定性，认为文章中对预测结果的表述不够准确和诚实，缺乏误差分析和置信区间。

补充讨论：

• **其他趣味性评论**：
   - [nixass] 和 [tboyd47] 的评论主要以幽默和调侃为主，未对主要讨论点提供实质性意见。
   - [mrlonglong] 询问文章是否给出了蒙古包的具体数量答案，显示出对结果的关注。

争议焦点：
• 模型的准确性和科学性是争议的核心，尤其是关于预测分数和模型验证的问题。
• 使用机器学习技术估算蒙古包数量的方法是否可靠，以及结果的解读是否准确。

I counted all of the yurts in Mongolia using machine learning
Jun 17, 2025
Table of Contents
The
Fall of Civilizations
podcast put out a
6¾-hour episode
on the history of the Mongol Empire, which I eagerly listened to. After finishing the episode I wondered
about contemporary Mongolian society, I wanted to learn what the lands that the Mongol Empire
exploded from are like in our current day. There are many ways to try to understand a society,
whether it be quantifying it or looking at the lived experiences within it. If you look at
data provided by the World Bank, you’ll see a country that has rapidly reduced poverty in the 21st
century, has a high economic growth rate, a healthy fertility rate, and is solidly an
upper-middle-income country. While Mongolia is a republic with a competitive party system,
Worldwide Governance Indicators
from the World Bank show a government that has issues with corruption, regulatory quality, and effectiveness.

(“Mongolia”)
All of these indicators are interesting to look at, but they don’t really show what a society is
like. I feel you get much more understanding by going to a country, walking the streets, and
talking to people there. If you’re unable to do this, the next best thing is spending hours
exploring Google Maps, which I did. I opened a satellite view of Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia.
I saw new glass buildings, Soviet-designed apartment blocks (called ugsarmal), impressive government
buildings, factories, and industrial areas. But something stood out to me. Yurts, extending for kilometers
in all directions.
Maps Data: Google © 2025 Airbus, CNES / Airbus, Maxar Technologies
Naturally, I was impressed by the quantity of yurts I saw, and I was curious: just how many yurts (ger in Mongolian) are in
Mongolia and why? This set me on the path drawing bounding boxes on over 10,000 yurts to train a machine learning
model to count the rest of the yurts in the country. While I was training the model, I wondered what
the story behind these yurts are, I did a small investigation for later in this article. For now,
this is the story of counting them.
Counting all the yurts in Mongolia
I was unable to find a count of the yurts in Mongolia, this left me with
the task of doing it myself. Although I had never studied or worked with machine learning, I knew
through some osmosis that machine learning is well fit for this task. I created a simple plan in my
brain:
Train a model to identify yurts
Reduce input space and parallelize searching of input space
Keep track of the yurts found
Training a model to identify yurts
The first thing I needed was training data, and lots of it. There’s many different options for satellite
imagery such as
Mapbox
,
Google Maps
,
and
ArcGIS
. I
decided to use Google Maps since I’m already familiar with it.
For digital maps, many systems break the world up into a series of 256 x 256 tiles identified by X, Y, Z values. This is
referred to as tiled web maps and allows for progressively loading maps at different zoom levels and
positions. The zoom level values tend to be 0 through 20, where 0 has the least tiles and 20 the
most. The formula for calculating the number of tiles at a given zoom (z) level is:
$2^z * 2^z$
.
This means increasing
z
by one will increase the tile count by four times.
I wrote a Python script that generated tiles from a box around Ulaanbaatar and downloaded
them to a folder to use as training data. To list the tiles inside a bounding box made up of a
southwest and northeast coordinates, I used the
mercantile package
.

.

Tiles from Google Maps, you can see yurts on the right tile. Maps Data: Google © 2025 Airbus, CNES / Airbus, Maxar Technologies
I decided to start at zoom level
17
as it is the lowest zoom level that I can still identify yurts
at. Once I downloaded several hundred tiles at this zoom level, I needed a way to label the yurts on
these tiles. Labeling is the process of drawing boxes around objects in an image. The idea is to
draw these boxes manually, creating what is called annotated data, and then training a model to do
the labeling using the annotated data.
There’s an open source tool called
Label Studio
that does just
this.
Here I drew bounding boxes on the tile around the yurts.

   - [nixass] 和 [tboyd47] 的评论主要以幽默和调侃为主，未对主要讨论点提供实质性意见。
   - [mrlonglong] 询问文章是否给出了蒙古包的具体数量答案，显示出对结果的关注。

争议焦点：
• 模型的准确性和科学性是争议的核心，尤其是关于预测分数和模型验证的问题。
• 使用机器学习技术估算蒙古包数量的方法是否可靠，以及结果的解读是否准确。

data.title: After millions of years, why are carnivorous plants still so small?
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: carnivorous plants have been trapping animals for millions of years, yet they have never evolved to become larger. These plants, which feed on meat and animal droppings, have independently evolved at least ten times in history. Despite their ability to capture prey, they remain small. The article explores the reasons behind their size limitation, suggesting it may be due to the trade-offs between the energy invested in capturing prey and the energy needed for overall growth. Additionally, their habitats often provide limited nutrients, which may also restrict their size. The evolutionary success of these plants lies in their specialized adaptations rather than their size.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： carnivorous plants（食肉植物）的演化、机制及其限制

不同观点：
• IAmBroom认为，维纳斯捕蝇草在贫瘠的土壤中进化出食肉特性，因为它们不需要强大的抗真菌防御机制。然而，当人类在土壤中添加营养物质时，这些植物容易受到真菌攻击而死亡。这表明它们适应了贫瘠环境，而在富营养环境下反而无法生存。
• _tom_不同意上述观点，指出一些植物（如荆棘）可以利用动物尸体作为肥料，并举了荆棘困住羊和椰子砸死动物的例子，说明植物可以从动物尸体中获益，即使它们并非直接捕食。
• jcalx引用了Worldbuilding Stack Exchange上的一个回答，描述了一种名为“Bonegrass”的假想食肉真菌，探讨了植物与真菌共生的可能性，暗示植物可能通过与真菌合作进化出更复杂的食肉机制。
• imoreno从进化生物学的角度分析，认为食肉植物的进化涉及多个适应峰，并且这些峰是随机且狭窄的。他还提出，食肉性对植物来说通常只是“副菜”，而非主要生存策略，因此广泛进化出食肉性的情况较少见。
• TheOtherHobbes分享了个人经验，提到自己养的维纳斯捕蝇草在短时间内捕获大量苍蝇，最终“撑死”了，说明这些植物在捕食方面非常高效。

补充讨论：
• Nevermark提出一个假设，认为植物可能会进化出以物理方式攻击和消耗其他植物的能力，从而获取养分和生存空间，并建议为此类植物行为创造新的名称。
• Several users (leoedin, bell-cot, chrisco255, bilsbie, Sevii, musicale) 讨论了食肉植物捕猎的物理限制、捕猎对象的大小（特别是较大动物）以及植物在缺乏蛋白质的情况下如何生存等问题。其中，leoedin和bell-cot提到较大动物会反击，从而限制了植物捕猎的规模，而Sevii指出植物由于无法咀嚼或撕裂猎物而处于劣势。

争议焦点：
• 核心争议在于食肉植物的进化条件和限制，特别是它们如何在不同环境中生存和适应。IAmBroom和_tom_的观点形成对比，一个强调贫瘠环境对食肉植物的必要性，另一个则指出植物可以通过其他方式从动物尸体中获益。

data.title: Show HN: Free local security checks for AI coding in VSCode, Cursor and Windsurf
data.author: jaimefjorge
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Codacy及相关AI工具在代码生成和质量控制中的应用与问题

不同观点：
• SkyPuncher：质疑在代码生成时运行Codacy相较于标准PR反馈的实际用例，担心LLM（大型语言模型）在处理问题时会导致"context pollution"（上下文污染），并提到曾因类似问题禁用了Cursor的"fix linter errors"功能。

• brynary：祝贺发布的同时，将该工具与Qlty CLI进行比较，并询问是否计划支持类似Claude Code等工具的CLI工作流。

• SpikedCola和samschooler：指出在Codacy网站的不同页面中，点击logo导致404错误链接的问题，属于用户体验方面的技术故障。

• godzillabrennus：分享了在AI生成代码项目中使用Codacy的初步计划，表示将尝试并反馈效果。

• romain_batlle：简单祝贺发布，未提出具体问题或意见。

• prophesi：询问该工具是否开源，以及MCP服务器是否可以在本地沙盒环境中运行。

• tosh：祝贺发布，并提出多个技术性问题，包括"guardrails"运行机制、扩展如何在diff视图中更改代码，以及是否兼容Claude Code和Amp等代理，还讨论了开发时运行guardrails与CI时运行的对比。

• rdevzw：尝试使用后发现AI生成的Python脚本中使用了带有CVE漏洞的requests库版本，强调AI生成代码的安全性问题，并表示将提供更多反馈。

补充讨论：
- 关于"context pollution"的讨论集中在SkyPuncher和tosh的评论中，反映了对LLM处理可能带来的负面影响的关注。
- 对工具兼容性和运行机制的讨论（brynary和tosh）显示出用户对扩展功能和集成其他AI工具的兴趣。
- 网站链接错误的反馈（SpikedCola和samschooler）虽然技术性不强，但指出了需要修复的用户体验问题。
- rdevzw的反馈提出了AI生成代码潜在的安全风险，这是一个重要的关注点。

争议焦点：
- 主要争议在于AI生成代码的可靠性和安全性（SkyPuncher和rdevzw的评论），以及如何有效避免或解决这些问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具在处理学术论文和内容消费中的作用及意义

不同观点：
• [jlarocco的观点] 认为AI工具在处理学术论文时只是浅层替代了浏览或阅读，无法让人真正吸收和理解内容。这种工具替代了内容创造和消费中的核心部分，使得人们可以假装自己创造了或理解了内容，但实际上并没有。这种做法显得毫无意义。

• [westurner的观点] 对AI工具持更积极的态度，详细介绍了诸如paperai、paperetl、PaperQA2和paperqa-zotero等工具的功能和应用场景。westurner强调了这些工具在处理和检索学术文章中的实际应用价值，如通过嵌入式索引和元数据存储来提高检索效率，并支持多种输入格式和数据库。

补充讨论：
• [jlarocco的批判性立场] 对AI工具替代人类在内容创造和消费中的角色持批判态度，认为这种替代缺乏意义，因为无法带来真正的理解和吸收。

• [westurner的技术性立场] 更关注AI工具的具体功能和实现方式，提供了多个相关项目的链接，展示了这些工具在科学研究中的潜在应用价值。

• [争议焦点] 主要在于AI工具在学术研究中是浅层替代还是有实质性帮助。jlarocco认为AI工具缺乏深度理解，而westurner则展示了这些工具在提高效率和便利性方面的潜力。

data.title: The Grug Brained Developer (2022)
data.author: smartmic
data.article_summary: 《Grug Brained Developer》是一本以幽默方式探讨软件开发思维的指南，作者自称为“头脑简单”的开发者，通过多年编程经验分享如何应对复杂性这一“恶魔”。Grug认为复杂性是软件开发的最大敌人，它悄无声息地进入代码库，使一切变得难以维护。应对复杂性的最佳武器是说“不”，拒绝不必要的功能和抽象。然而，现实中有时要说“好”以获取报酬，建议采用80/20原则，实现最有效用的解决方案，避免复杂性扩散。代码重构也很重要，但不要过早进行，应等待系统结构自然显现。本书旨在帮助开发者在保持理智的同时，享受编程的乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的调试、复杂性管理、工具选择以及LLM（大型语言模型）的使用

不同观点：
• **调试工具 vs. 打印语句调试**：[titanomachy] 认为使用调试器是理解系统的高效方式，但其团队中很少有人使用调试器，大多数人依赖打印语句调试。他强调调试器在理解代码调用栈方面的优势，并建议新手学习使用调试器。

• **复杂性的本质**：[prmph] 认为复杂性是非常有害的，应该通过深思熟虑来简化问题，避免不必要的复杂性。他提供了多个例子，如简化TypeScript类型、替换ESLint为Biome.js等。相反，[0xbadcafebee] 则认为复杂性本身不是坏事，只要其有用且必要，复杂性只是意味着“需要多方面考虑”，过度简化也可能带来问题。

• **复杂性的管理与决策**：[osigurdson] 指出人们对复杂性缺乏统一的理解，有时“复杂”只是“坏”的代名词。他质疑诸如“多个文件是否意味着复杂”等问题。而[GMoromisato] 则讨论了现代软件开发中，为了节省时间而引入复杂性可能带来的风险，如过早抽象、复杂类型以及泄漏的抽象等问题。

• **LLM在开发中的应用**：[mcqueenjordan] 提到利用LLM模拟“grug-brained开发者”来评论当前问题是一种很好的减压方式。[1-more] 则以一种幽默的方式表达了对静态类型、纯函数式语言的偏好，认为这些工具能帮助避免处理副作用的问题。

补充讨论：
• **对特定技术或方法的赞赏**：[butterlesstoast] 表达了对教授Carson及HTMX技术的感谢，认为这些技术在实际工作中展现了巨大价值。而[anthomtb] 引用了对微服务复杂性的批评，认为过度复杂化往往得不偿失。

• **对“架构师”和“萨满”的批评**：[ethbr1] 批评了不直接参与实现的“架构师”和“萨满”，认为这些人脱离了实际工作，导致项目无法顺利推进。

争议的焦点：
• **复杂性的定义与处理**：一部分人认为复杂性是需要极力避免的，而另一部分人则认为复杂性是不可避免的，应该根据具体情况判断其价值。

44303542.article_summary: 《Grug Brained Developer》是一本以幽默方式探讨软件开发思维的指南，作者自称为“头脑简单”的开发者，通过多年编程经验分享如何应对复杂性这一“恶魔”。Grug认为复杂性是软件开发的最大敌人，它悄无声息地进入代码库，使一切变得难以维护。应对复杂性的最佳武器是说“不”，拒绝不必要的功能和抽象。然而，现实中有时要说“好”以获取报酬，建议采用80/20原则，实现最有效用的解决方案，避免复杂性扩散。代码重构也很重要，但不要过早进行，应等待系统结构自然显现。本书旨在帮助开发者在保持理智的同时，享受编程的乐趣。
44303542.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发中的调试、复杂性管理、工具选择以及LLM（大型语言模型）的使用

不同观点：
• **调试工具 vs. 打印语句调试**：[titanomachy] 认为使用调试器是理解系统的高效方式，但其团队中很少有人使用调试器，大多数人依赖打印语句调试。他强调调试器在理解代码调用栈方面的优势，并建议新手学习使用调试器。

• **复杂性的本质**：[prmph] 认为复杂性是非常有害的，应该通过深思熟虑来简化问题，避免不必要的复杂性。他提供了多个例子，如简化TypeScript类型、替换ESLint为Biome.js等。相反，[0xbadcafebee] 则认为复杂性本身不是坏事，只要其有用且必要，复杂性只是意味着“需要多方面考虑”，过度简化也可能带来问题。

• **复杂性的管理与决策**：[osigurdson] 指出人们对复杂性缺乏统一的理解，有时“复杂”只是“坏”的代名词。他质疑诸如“多个文件是否意味着复杂”等问题。而[GMoromisato] 则讨论了现代软件开发中，为了节省时间而引入复杂性可能带来的风险，如过早抽象、复杂类型以及泄漏的抽象等问题。

• **LLM在开发中的应用**：[mcqueenjordan] 提到利用LLM模拟“grug-brained开发者”来评论当前问题是一种很好的减压方式。[1-more] 则以一种幽默的方式表达了对静态类型、纯函数式语言的偏好，认为这些工具能帮助避免处理副作用的问题。

补充讨论：
• **对特定技术或方法的赞赏**：[butterlesstoast] 表达了对教授Carson及HTMX技术的感谢，认为这些技术在实际工作中展现了巨大价值。而[anthomtb] 引用了对微服务复杂性的批评，认为过度复杂化往往得不偿失。

• **对“架构师”和“萨满”的批评**：[ethbr1] 批评了不直接参与实现的“架构师”和“萨满”，认为这些人脱离了实际工作，导致项目无法顺利推进。

争议的焦点：
• **复杂性的定义与处理**：一部分人认为复杂性是需要极力避免的，而另一部分人则认为复杂性是不可避免的，应该根据具体情况判断其价值。

data.title: My iPhone 8 Refuses to Die: Now It's a Solar-Powered Vision OCR Server
data.author: hemant6488
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者如何将一台闲置的iPhone 8改造成由太阳能供电的光学字符识别（OCR）服务器。该设备运行一个SwiftUI应用，利用苹果的Vision框架处理OCR请求，并通过EcoFlow River 2 Pro和220W太阳能板供电，实现了离网运行。在一年多的时间里，它处理了83,418次OCR请求和48GB的图像数据，为作者节省了每月约7-10美元的电费。

尽管从成本角度看，这种设置并非最实际的选择，但作者通过该项目获得了对太阳能管理和iOS开发的深入了解，并且拥有了一个有趣的展示品。硬件包括一台作为网页服务器的迷你电脑、iPhone 8和EcoFlow River 2 Pro。整个系统通过Tailscale网络连接，实现实时监控和数据处理。虽然更简单的解决方案存在，但作者更享受这种动手实验的过程。

My iPhone 8 Refuses to Die: Now It’s a Solar-Powered Vision OCR Server
#
After running for over a year, my solar-powered iPhone 8 has processed
83,418 OCR requests
and
48GB of images
using nothing but Apple’s Vision framework and renewable energy. Most people toss their old iPhones in a drawer when they upgrade. Me? I turned mine into a 24/7 OCR server that’s been saving me $7-10/month while running completely off-grid.
And yes, before you ask - I could have just run this on my Mac like a normal person, but where’s the fun in that?
TL;DR - Technical Summary
#
The Setup:
iPhone 8 running SwiftUI app with Apple Vision OCR
EcoFlow River 2 Pro (768Wh) + 220W solar panel
Mini PC handling web services and API routing
Tailscale network connecting everything
Performance Stats:
83,418 total OCR requests processed
48GB of image data handled
1000+ requests on busy days
76% battery health after 1+ year of 24/7 operation
$7-10/month electricity savings vs grid power
Key Learnings:
Apple Vision framework is surprisingly accurate for local OCR
iPhone 8 hardware is incredibly reliable for server workloads
Solar power works great with 8+ hours of sun most of the year
Local processing beats cloud services for privacy and cost at scale
Why Would You Even Do This?
#
Short Answer:
I don’t know, I love renewable energy and I love to tinker.
The Logical Approach
#
So I’ve got this image-heavy personal project that chews through hundreds of images daily, categorizing them automatically. It’s been happily humming along for over a year now. Any
reasonable
person would just run the OCR processing on their Mac - Apple’s Vision framework works great on macOS after all (maybe slightly better even than on iOS).
The “Me” Approach
#
But I’m not logical. I see a perfectly good iPhone 8 and think:
“You know what this needs? A second career as a solar-powered image processing servant."
(If this sounds familiar, it’s because I have a
track record of giving old devices second lives
- my Kindle Paperwhite is now a weather dashboard.)
The real catalyst?
My EcoFlow River 2 Pro was sitting idle between camping trips. My OCR server was already running on grid power, but switching to solar felt like the natural evolution.
The Benefits I Didn’t Expect
#
Real-time dashboard
on my window sill while bird watching
Grid independence
for my personal projects
Actual savings
: $7.21 (May) + $8.82 (April) = exactly my $7-10/month estimate
Amazing conversation starter
when people visit
“Is it practical? Debatable. Is it cool? Absolutely."
Bottom line:
Probably not worth it from pure cost perspective, but I’m now I have a cool thing to show people.
What Exactly Is This Thing?
#
Here’s my delightfully over-engineered (or under-engineered, depending on how you look at it) setup:
Mini PC
running my web server, image processing service, plex server, a few archive warriors, and god knows what else (because why keep things simple?)
iPhone 8
perched on my window sill, running a vibe-coded SwiftUI app that serves as both OCR processor and real-time dashboard
EcoFlow River 2 Pro
powering both devices (living that off-grid life, one image at a time)
Tailscale network
connecting everything together (because local networks are for peasants but mainly so that it works on cellular as well)
The workflow is beautifully ridiculous: My image processing service fetches the images and sends them to my iPhone 8 for OCR processing using Apple’s Vision framework. The iPhone processes the text, sends it back, and updates its dashboard with processing stats. All while I watch birds outside my window and feel smug about my setup.
Could I have just run this entire thing on my Mac? Yes. Would it have been more efficient? Absolutely. Would I have learned as much about solar power management and iOS development? Definitely not. And would I have this amazing conversation starter when people visit? Not a chance.

#
The EcoFlow River 2 Pro Choice
#

data.title: Show HN: Delve, an open source (AGPL) enterprise-grade data analytics platform
data.author: ilovetux
data.article_summary: Delve是一个企业级数据分析平台，目前处于Alpha预发布阶段。它支持交互式搜索、自定义仪表盘、实时警报等多种功能，并通过REST API、文件上传和Syslog等方式进行数据整合。平台采用GNU AGPLv3许可证，允许自由使用、修改和分发，但需公开网络修改版本的源代码。安装过程简单，通过复制示例配置文件、创建数据库和运行测试即可启动。平台提供详细的文档和手动指南，帮助用户进行部署和系统管理。开发者可以通过克隆仓库并按照指定步骤配置开发环境。

Delve - Enterprise Data Analytics Platform

: Delve is in Alpha pre-release. Please try it out and provide feedback of any issues or missing features you encounter, but production use is discouraged at the moment.
License
Delve is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPL-3.0).
This means:
You are free to use, modify, and distribute this software, provided that any network-accessible modifications are also made available under the same license.
The full license text is available in the
LICENSE
file and at
https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html
.
If you deploy a modified version of Delve on a server and allow users to interact with it over a network, you must also make the source code of your modified version available to those users.
For more information, see the
GNU AGPL FAQ
.
Please use the Issues section of this repository for feature requests, bug reports, and general feedback.
Overview
Delve is an enterprise-grade platform for ingesting, analyzing, and deriving insights from any data source. Key capabilities include:
Data Integration
REST API endpoints
Syslog receiver (UDP/TCP/TLS)
File monitoring and ingestion
Direct uploads
Analysis & Visualization
Interactive search interface
Pipeline-based query language
Custom dashboards
Real-time alerts
Enterprise Features
Role-based access control
Custom app development
API-first architecture
Extensible search commands
Scheduled tasks and automation
Installation
Download one of the pre-built zip files from the
releases page
.
Unzip the file in the desired location.
That's it!
Initial Setup
After installation, setup can be as simple or as complex as you need.
The simplest setup involves using the default settings. The default settings are designed to be most useful to someone who is looking to quickly ingest some data (like log files or a REST API) and would like to search, transform, correlate, store, or otherwise interact with that data.
This use-case can be quite handy if you need to quickly troubleshoot an issue or would like to crawl a REST API for information.
To start using Delve with the simplest setup, use the following commands:
#
Copy the example settings and urls files
cp ./delve/example-settings.py ./delve/settings.py
cp ./delve/example-urls.py ./delve/urls.py
#
Create the database
./dl migrate
#
Run the tests
./dl
test
#
Create an admin user
./dl createsuperuser
#
Start serving the web UI
./dl serve
#
In another window, you can start the task runner
./dl qcluster
Documentation
Admin Manual
: Deployment, configuration, and system administration
User Manual
: Search syntax, dashboards, and data analysis
API Documentation: Available at
/api/docs
after installation
Configuration
Configuration settings are located in

data.title: A different take on S-expressions
data.author: tearflake
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了一种S-expression（符号表达式）的特殊规范文档，目标读者是编程初学者。S-expression是一种用于表示嵌套列表数据结构和代码的记法，常见于Lisp语言家族。本文档描述的S-expr库在传统原子和列表处理基础上，增加了对字符串、注释和转置块的特殊处理。

1. **介绍**：S-expressions是计算机科学和编程语言理论的基础概念，常用于表示代码和数据。
2. **非正式定义**：S-expression可以是原子或S-expression的列表，列表可以嵌套，表示复杂层次结构。
3. **字符串、注释和转置块**：
   - **字符串**：单行或多行，多行字符串使用`"""`包围，需注意修改时的对齐。
   - **注释**：使用`/`而非`"`，单行和多行注释均支持，多行注释也用`///`包围。
   - **转置块**：代码块中行和列对角互换位置，支持水平和垂直缩进，以二维空间表示代码。

通过这些扩展，S-expr增强了代码的可读性和表达能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对S-expressions引入2D结构及相关语法的讨论

不同观点：
• [反对引入2D结构] phoe-krk认为，传统的S-expressions是线性读取且忽略大部分空白，而引入2D结构违反了这一设计原则。例如，要求在读取TRD-ATOM前必须完整读取多行字符串，以及读取函数需要上下跳动来解析结构。phoe-krk还指出新结构的可读性未必更好，并认为这种复杂性没有正当理由。drob518也明确表示不接受这种改变。

• [支持扩展和创新的可能性] chc4认为这些扩展是可以加到S-expressions中的，没有异议。jazzyjackson则提到了JSONification的尝试，以及对不同语法符号的探索，例如使用[straight]和{curly}区分数组和对象。此外，jazzyjackson还提出了垂直排版的可能性，类似于日语的写法。

• [其他语言的参考] fn-mote提到Racket有一个2D语法模式，允许以不同方式编程表格，这与S-expressions不同但相关。

• [简化语法] somewhereoutth建议去掉括号，例如将(eq (mul (a a)) (pow (a 2)))简化为eq mul a a pow a 2。

• [S-expressions的局限] TOGoS认为S-expressions的问题不在于语法，而在于无法直接表示非列表的对象，需要在S-expressions上发明额外的表示层或使用扩展语法，从而失去其简洁性。TOGoS建议引入类似JSON的语法来直接表示复杂数据结构。

补充讨论：
• [争议的焦点] 主要集中在是否应该对S-expressions进行2D结构或其他形式的扩展，反对者认为这会增加不必要的复杂性，而支持者则认为探索新语法和扩展是有价值的。

• [幽默和怀疑态度] 一些评论如pkilgore和stray对文章的严肃性表示怀疑，认为可能是个玩笑，而phoe-krk则直接表达了对文章的不满。

• [实际应用] jazzyjackson和TOGoS都提到了实际项目中的需求和解决方案，如事件循环和错误处理，这些讨论提供了对S-expressions扩展需求的实际背景。

s-expr.md
S-expr
[about document]
Peculiar kind of S-expressions specification document
[intended audience]
beginners in programming
table of contents
1. introduction
2. informal definition
3. strings, comments, and transposed blocks
4. conclusion
1. introduction
S-expressions (Symbolic Expressions) are a fundamental concept in computer science and programming language theory. S-expressions are a simple, yet powerful notation for representing nested list data structures and code in a parenthesized form. They are commonly associated with the Lisp family of programming languages, where they serve both as a way to represent code and data uniformly.
S-expr
is a S-expression parsing library. Other than usual treatment of atoms and lists, it features peculiar decisions in syntax definition regarding strings, comments, and transposed blocks of contents.
2. informal definition
The general form of an S-expression is either:
An atom (e.g.,
atom
), or
A list of S-expressions (e.g.,
(expr1 expr2 expr3)
).
Lists can be nested, allowing for the representation of complex hierarchical structures. For example:
(eq (mul x x) (pow x 2))
This S-expression depicts equality between multiplication and square.
3. strings, comments and transposed blocks
Although a great part of S-expressions power lies in its simplicity, let's introduce a few extensions in a hope of making expressed code more readable, namely: strings, comments, and transposed blocks.
strings
Strings in
S-expr
may be single-line or multi-line. Single-line strings are atoms enclosed in
"..."
pairs, like in expression
"this is a single-line string"
, and represent Unicode format strings. Multi-line strings are enclosed between an odd number greater than 1 of
"
symbols in the following manner:
"""
this is a
multi-line
string
"""
Enclosing between a pair of
"""
symbols, multi-line strings are bound in a rectangle between the start of the first
"""
symbol, and the end of the second
"""
symbol. Remember to be careful when modifying contents of multi-line strings to make sure that the end of the second
"""
symbol is always placed horizontally behind the longest line in the string.
Notice that it is also possible to write expressions like:
(fst-atom """   trd-atom)
00001
00002
00003
"""
where the expression stands for three atoms in a list.
comments
Comment expressions are ignored by the system, and they serve as notes to help programmers reading their code. They are parsed just like strings, only using the
/
instead of the
"
symbol. Thus, a single-line comment may be written as
/this is a single-line comment/
, and may appear repeatedly wherever a whitespace is expected. An example of a multi-line comment may be:
///
this is a
multi-line
comment
///
Just like strings enclosing between a pair of
"""
symbols, multi-line comments are bound in a rectangle between the start of the first
///
symbol, and the end of the second
///
symbol. Notice that it is also possible to write expressions like:
///
00001 (
00002   fst-atom
00003   snd-atom
00004   trd-atom
00005 )
///
where the expression stands for three atoms in a list.
transposed blocks
Transposed blocks are something new and unusual in the world of S-expression parsing. They represent blocks of code where rows and columns diagonally swap their places. Naturally, vertically spanned S-expressions have ability to horizontally indent their contents. Analogously, Transposed blocks span horizontally, and have ability to vertically indent their contents, thus using two-dimensional space in a diagonally mirrored manner.
For example, the expression:
(eq (mul (a a)) (pow (a 2)))
may be also written with horizontal indenting as:
(
eq
(
mul
(
a
a
)
)
(
pow
(
a
2
)
)
)
which, in turn, may be transposed using
*
symbol sequences as in the following example:
* (                               )
*   e (           ) (           )
*   q   m (     )     p (     )     *
u   a a       o   a 2       *
l             w             *
Tran

data.title: Think of a Number
data.author: IdealeZahlen
data.article_summary: 文章作者批评了对AGI（人工通用智能）的过度炒作，特别是Sam Altman等人的言论。作者认为当前的AI在本科数学水平上表现良好，但这并不代表真正的AGI，因为AI无法在博士级别的数学研究中独立思考和提出新证明。现有的数学数据库主要集中在本科或奥林匹克水平，无法代表真正的研究数学。作者计划创建一个包含高难度数论问题的秘密数据库，以测试AI在更高水平数学中的能力。他呼吁数论研究者提供帮助，共同收集至少20个超出本科水平的问题，以进行更真实的AI能力测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在处理高级数学论文方面的能力及其局限性

不同观点：
• AnotherGoodName认为，AI在处理高级数学论文时表现不佳，尤其是面对高度精炼的数学语言和复杂的理论（如ABC猜想）时，AI无法提供准确的注释和数值示例。他指出，AI常常依赖于已有的在线资源，无法独立处理新的或极为专业的内容。
• Jenny91指出，数学领域非常广泛，问题的难度往往取决于具体领域和问题的定义。她认为，虽然LLM（大型语言模型）有其局限性，但在某些方面仍然可以加速数学研究。她强调，AI不会使数学家失业，但在某些任务上可以发挥作用。
• Prats226则关注到公开问题可能会被AI“污染”，即一旦问题被AI处理过，它们就不能再用于测试，因为答案可能已经泄露。

补充讨论：
• AnotherGoodName通过具体例子（如Inter-universal Teichmüller理论）说明了AI在理解和解释高级数学概念方面的不足。
• Jenny91提出了几个不同的问题，分别讨论了AI的局限性和潜力，强调了在特定领域和任务上，AI的能力是有限的，但在某些情况下仍然有用。
• Prats226指出了一个实际问题，即如何处理公开数据集以避免被AI“污染”，这涉及到AI测试和研究方法的科学性。

• AI在处理高级数学论文时的能力极限以及如何有效利用AI来辅助数学研究。
• 公开问题被AI处理后的“污染”问题，这涉及到AI测试数据集的有效性和科学性。

44282000.article_content:
My feed was recently clogged up with news articles reporting that Sam Altman thinks that AGI is here, or will be here next year, or whatever. I will refrain from giving even more air to this nonsense by linking to the stories. This kind of irresponsible hype-generation drives me nuts (although it also drives up stock prices so I can see why the tech bros are motivated to do it). Sure AI can have a good crack at undergraduate mathematics right now, and sure that’s pretty amazing. But our universities are full of students who can also have a good crack at undergraduate mathematics so in some sense we have achieved very little (and certainly nothing which is of any use to me as a working mathematician in 2025). If AI cannot do mathematics at PhD-student level (i.e., if it can’t start thinking for itself) then AGI is certainly not here, whatever “AGI” even means.
In an attempt to move beyond the hype and to focus on where we are right now, I’m going to try an experiment. It might fail. But if you’re a number theorist reading this, you can help me make it succeed.
Can AI do mathematics?
The null hypothesis as far as I am concerned is “not really”. More precisely, I have seen absolutely no evidence that language models are doing anything other than paraphrasing and attempting to generalise what they’ve seen on the internet, not always correctly. Don’t get me wrong — this gets you a long way! Indeed many undergraduate mathematics exams at university level are designed so that students who have a basic knowledge of the ideas in the course will pass the exam. The exam will test this knowledge by asking the student either to regurgitate the ideas, or to apply them in situations analogous to those seen in the problem sheets which came with the course. You can pass these exams by intelligent pattern-matching (if you have an encyclopedic knowledge of the material, which a machine would have). Furthermore, undergraduate pure mathematics is
stagnant
. The courses (other than my Lean course) which we teach in the pure mathematics degree at Imperial College London are essentially exactly the same as those which were offered to me when I was an undergraduate in Cambridge in the late 1980s, and very little post-1960 mathematics is taught at undergraduate level, even at the top institutions in the world, because it simply takes too long to get there. This is exactly why language models can pass undergraduate mathematics exams. But as I already said,
this is no use to me
as a working mathematician and it is certainly not AGI.
How do we test AI?
If you look at currently available mathematics databases, they are essentially all focused on mathematics which is at undergraduate or olympiad-style level. Perhaps the tech bros are deluded in thinking that because their models are getting high marks on such databases then they’re doing well. I want to firstly stress the fundamental notion that these databases are
completely unrepresentative of mathematics
. More recently we had the
FrontierMath dataset
, which was designed by mathematicians and which looked like a real step in the right direction, even though the answers to the questions were not proofs or ideas, but just numbers (which is also a long way from what research mathematics looks like); the dataset is private, but the 5 sample questions which were revealed to us were clearly beyond undergraduate level. People (including me) were tricked into saying publically that any machine which can do something nontrivial here would really be a breakthrough. The next thing we know, OpenAI were claiming that their system could get 25 percent on this database. Oof. But shortly after that, Epoch AI (who put he dataset together) revealed that 25 percent of the questions were undergraduate or olympiad level, and this week it transpires that OpenAI were
behind the funding of the dataset
and reportedly were even given access to some of the questions (added later: in fact Elliot Glazer from Epoch AI has
confirmed this on Reddit
); all of a sudden 25 percent doesn’t sound so great any more.
So maybe we need to do it all again
Let’s make a database
I want people (i.e. researchers in number theory at PhD level or beyond) to help me put together a secret database of hard number theory problems. I already have 5 but I need at least 20 and ideally far more, so I need help. The problems need to be beyond undergraduate level in the sense that undergraduates will not have been taught all the skills necessary to solve them. Because LLMs are not up to writing proofs, the answers unfortunately need to be non-negative integers: there is simply no point asking an LLM basic research level questions and then ploughing through the crap they produce and giving it 0/10; anyone who thinks that LLMs are actually capable of writing proofs should show me one that can do the Putnam because all efforts I saw on the 2024 exam were abysmal and this is undergraduate level: as always, the difficulty here is that soon after

data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary:
本文总结了Anthropic公司在构建大型语言模型（LLM）代理方面的经验和建议。文章指出，最成功的代理实现通常使用简单、可组合的模式，而非复杂的框架。文中区分了**工作流**和**代理**两种系统架构：工作流通过预定义的代码路径来协调LLM和工具，而代理则由LLM动态指导自身进程和工具使用。

文章建议，在构建LLM应用时，应寻找最简单的解决方案，只有在必要时才增加复杂性。工作流适用于预定义任务，提供可预测性和一致性；而代理则适合需要灵活性和大规模模型驱动决策的场景。

文中还介绍了常见的代理系统模式，包括增强型LLM（具备检索、工具和记忆功能）和提示链工作流。并提醒开发者，尽量直接使用LLM API，以保持简单和易于调试。如果使用框架，需理解其底层代码以避免错误。

Engineering at Anthropic
Building effective agents
Published
Dec 19, 2024
We've worked with dozens of teams building LLM agents across industries. Consistently, the most successful implementations use simple, composable patterns rather than complex frameworks.
Over the past year, we've worked with dozens of teams building large language model (LLM) agents across industries. Consistently, the most successful implementations weren't using complex frameworks or specialized libraries. Instead, they were building with simple, composable patterns.
In this post, we share what we’ve learned from working with our customers and building agents ourselves, and give practical advice for developers on building effective agents.
What are agents?
"Agent" can be defined in several ways. Some customers define agents as fully autonomous systems that operate independently over extended periods, using various tools to accomplish complex tasks. Others use the term to describe more prescriptive implementations that follow predefined workflows. At Anthropic, we categorize all these variations as
agentic systems
, but draw an important architectural distinction between
workflows
and
agents
:
Workflows
are systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths.
Agents
, on the other hand, are systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks.
Below, we will explore both types of agentic systems in detail. In Appendix 1 (“Agents in Practice”), we describe two domains where customers have found particular value in using these kinds of systems.
When (and when not) to use agents
When building applications with LLMs, we recommend finding the simplest solution possible, and only increasing complexity when needed. This might mean not building agentic systems at all. Agentic systems often trade latency and cost for better task performance, and you should consider when this tradeoff makes sense.
When more complexity is warranted, workflows offer predictability and consistency for well-defined tasks, whereas agents are the better option when flexibility and model-driven decision-making are needed at scale. For many applications, however, optimizing single LLM calls with retrieval and in-context examples is usually enough.
When and how to use frameworks
There are many frameworks that make agentic systems easier to implement, including:
LangGraph
from LangChain;
Amazon Bedrock's
AI Agent framework
;
Rivet
, a drag and drop GUI LLM workflow builder; and
Vellum
, another GUI tool for building and testing complex workflows.
These frameworks make it easy to get started by simplifying standard low-level tasks like calling LLMs, defining and parsing tools, and chaining calls together. However, they often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts ​​and responses, making them harder to debug. They can also make it tempting to add complexity when a simpler setup would suffice.
We suggest that developers start by using LLM APIs directly: many patterns can be implemented in a few lines of code. If you do use a framework, ensure you understand the underlying code. Incorrect assumptions about what's under the hood are a common source of customer error.
See our
cookbook
for some sample implementations.
Building blocks, workflows, and agents
In this section, we’ll explore the common patterns for agentic systems we’ve seen in production. We'll start with our foundational building block—the augmented LLM—and progressively increase complexity, from simple compositional workflows to autonomous agents.
Building block: The augmented LLM
The basic building block of agentic systems is an LLM enhanced with augmentations such as retrieval, tools, and memory. Our current models can actively use these capabilities—generating their own search queries, selecting appropriate tools, and determining what information to retain.
The augmented LLM
We recommend focusing on two key aspects of the implementation: tailoring these capabilities to your specific use case and ensuring they provide an easy, well-documented interface for your LLM. While there are many ways to implement these augmentations, one approach is through our recently released
Model Context Protocol
, which allows developers to integrate with a growing ecosystem of third-party tools with a simple
client implementation
.
For the remainder of this post, we'll assume each LLM call has access to these augmented capabilities.
Workflow: Prompt chaining
Prompt chaining decomposes a task into a sequence of steps, where each LLM call processes the output of the previous one. You can add programmatic checks (see "gate” in the diagram below) on any intermediate steps to ensure that the process is still on track.

文章建议，在构建LLM应用时，应寻找最简单的解决方案，只有在必要时才增加复杂性。工作流适用于预定义任务，提供可预测性和一致性；而代理则适合需要灵活性和大规模模型驱动决策的场景。

文中还介绍了常见的代理系统模式，包括增强型LLM（具备检索、工具和记忆功能）和提示链工作流。并提醒开发者，尽量直接使用LLM API，以保持简单和易于调试。如果使用框架，需理解其底层代码以避免错误。
44301809.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于AI代理（AI agents）的文章及其相关技术实践的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• **支持文章的观点**（simonw, gregorymichael）：simonw认为文章清晰定义了“AI代理”的概念，并区分了“代理”和“工作流”，提供了有用的模式描述。gregorymichael也赞同文章的观点，指出文章强调了不一定要使用复杂的代理系统，简单的确定性工作流往往更有效。
• **代理开发的实际挑战**（suninsight, AvAn12）：suninsight提到在实际生产环境中，使用代理框架（如Langraph）可能不切实际，最终他们不得不从头开始构建系统。AvAn12则关注代理在并发任务处理、任务排队和竞争条件等方面可能面临的设计挑战。
• **代理技术的瓶颈与 hype 回落**（chaosprint, suyash）：chaosprint认为代理技术的发展遇到了瓶颈，甚至最新的技术（如gemini）也出现了倒退。suyash也认为代理技术的热潮已经过去。
• **代理的实际应用与价值**（i_love_retros, laurentiurad）：i_love_retros质疑是否有代理在生产环境中真正节省了成本并完成了有价值的工作。laurentiurad分享了自己的经验，使用文章中的工作流设置成本高且响应慢，因此选择继续使用传统搜索方法。

补充讨论：
• **简单与复杂的平衡**（Zaylan, btbuildem）：Zaylan建议从最简单的有效方案开始，避免过度复杂化。btbuildem支持“做一件事并做好”的原则，强调可组合模式的重要性。
• **非技术人员的理解需求**（bredren）：bredren认为应该提供非技术版本的指南，以帮助非技术人员理解和应用代理技术。
• **对文章技术内容的反馈**（evertedsphere, bgwalter）：evertedsphere对文章的页面排版提出了改进建议。bgwalter则对文章内容及其技术性描述持怀疑态度，认为可能只是一种技术潮流。

争议焦点：
• 代理技术在实际应用中的有效性和实用价值存在争议。一些评论者（如suninsight, laurentiurad）基于实际经验对其可行性提出质疑，而另一些评论者（如simonw, gregorymichael）则认可文章的理论价值和技术指导。

data.title: Honda conducts successful launch and landing of experimental reusable rocket
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，本田研发公司成功进行了自主研发的可重复使用火箭的发射与着陆测试。火箭长6.3米，直径85厘米，干重900公斤，湿重1,312公斤，在北海道大树町的设施中完成了此次测试。火箭升至271.4米高度，并在飞行56.6秒后精准降落在预定地点37厘米范围内，验证了火箭在升空与降落过程中的飞行稳定性和着陆能力等关键技术。测试期间，本田采取了严格的安全措施，设立了半径1公里的禁入区域，并确保火箭不会偏离预定飞行轨道。本田自2021年起开始火箭技术研究，旨在通过发射卫星等应用，创造新的太空价值，满足未来对卫星发射火箭的需求。

不同观点：
• **关于创新的讨论**：
  - [ItCouldBeWorse] 认为，很多技术创新其实是营销推动的，所谓的“创新者”并不总是第一个计划做这件事的人，而是被市场竞争和营销压力驱动的结果。例子包括虚幻引擎团队因为竞争对手的渲染图而开发了新的反射技术。
  - [Daisywh] 则对Honda进入火箭领域感到惊喜，认为这种跨界创新正是科技的魅力所在，Honda的工程技术可能会为太空探索带来新的突破。

• **关于技术实现的讨论**：
  - [whatever1] 提问是否因为芯片计算能力的提升，使得建造可重复使用火箭变得更加容易，暗示技术进步推动了太空探索的进展。

  - [romain_batlle] 提出Honda可能在2026年用喷气发动机替代F1电动引擎，以提高可靠性，涉及到技术移植和跨领域应用的可能性。

• **关于Honda火箭实用性的争议**：
  - [leesec] 认为Honda火箭虽然成功发射，但距离实际应用还有很长的路，并且在时间上已经比其他公司落后十年以上，表现出对Honda技术进展的怀疑。
  - [cududa] 对火箭是否是首次发射提出疑问，并询问是否存在之前的失败尝试，表现出对信息透明度的关注。

补充讨论：
• **市场竞争的全球影响**：
  - [walterbell] 认为Honda的参与是日本航天工业的一小步，但却是全球航天行业竞争的一大步，暗示Honda的加入可能会改变行业格局。
  - [RataNova] 对Honda是否会进一步推动亚轨道发射表示好奇，涉及到对未来技术发展的预测和期待。

• **个人感性评论**：
  - [EvanAnderson] 通过自己妻子旧Honda Civic车的例子，表达了对Honda耐用性和可靠性的认可，并幽默地表示期待Honda硬件未来能真正送东西上月球。

争议焦点：Honda火箭的技术创新性和实用性，以及其在行业中的竞争力和未来发展潜力。

Honda Conducts Successful Launch and Landing Test of Experimental Reusable Rocket
TOKYO, Japan, June 17, 2025 â Honda R&D Co., Ltd., a research and development subsidiary of Honda Motor Co., Ltd., today conducted a launch and landing test of an experimental reusable rocket
*1
(6.3 m in length, 85 cm in diameter, 900 kg dry weight/1,312 kg wet weight) developed independently by Honda. The test was completed successfully, the first time Honda landed a rocket after reaching an altitude of nearly 300 meters.
This test marked the first launch and landing test conducted by Honda with an aim to demonstrate key technologies essential for rocket reusability, such as flight stability during ascent and descent, as well as landing capability. Through this successful test, Honda achieved its intended rocket behaviors for the launch and landing (reaching an altitude of 271.4 m, and landing within 37cm of the target touchdown point, with a flight duration of 56.6 sec), while obtaining data during the ascent and descent.

*2
, Hiroo District, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan

Test being conducted in Taiki Town in Hokkaido, Japan(Photo taken in May, 2025)
Launch and landing test
*1 A reusable rocket, also known as a reusable launch vehicle (RLV), is a type of rocket that, unlike a conventional expendable launch vehicle (ELV), can be used repeatedly in a short period of time. A reusable rocket is launched in a vertical position, reaches an altitude of around 100 kilometers, and then lands back on earth while maintaining a vertical position.
*2 Taiki Town, located in southeastern Hokkaido, Japan, has been developing itself as a âspace townâ through the joint efforts of public and private sectors, and various aviation/space related tests are being conducted by a wide range of organizations including JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), businesses and universities.
ï¼Safety measures for Honda rocket testingï¼
Since 2024, Honda has been safely conducting engine combustion tests and hovering tests for its reusable rockets in Taiki Town in Hiroo District, Hokkaido, Japan. As with all previous tests, Honda conducted this launch and landing test while placing the highest priority on safety and with the understanding and cooperation of local authorities and residents.Â
Specific safety measures taken for this test
A restricted area with a 1-kilometer radius was established. During the test, access to the area was restricted through the installation of signs and gates, as well as the deployment of security personnel.
The restricted area was defined by calculating the potential area where the rocket could fall to earth in the event of a thrust cut-off and by adding a sufficient buffer zone (safe distance calculated based on the guidelines set forth by the Cabinet Office of the Government of Japan) that would cover the potential area where a blast wave, debris dispersion, or fireballs could impact in the event of an explosion within the potential fall area.
The experimental rocket was equipped with a safety system to prevent deviation from a pre-defined flight corridor, speed and attitude conditions, ensuring no impact beyond the restricted area.

As announced in 2021, Honda has been pursuing research and development in the field of space technologies while viewing it as a place to take on challenges to realize the âdreamsâ and âpotentialâ of people worldwide while leveraging its core technologies. Honda has the aim to enable people to transcend the constraints of time, place or ability and make peopleâs daily lives more enjoyable. Examples of Honda initiatives toward creating new value in the ultimate environment of outer space include research into a circulative renewable energy system, key robotic technologies for use in outer space and reusable rockets.Â

data.title: OpenSERDES – Open Hardware Serializer/Deserializer (SerDes) in Verilog (2020)
data.author: peter_d_sherman
data.article_summary: OpenSERDES 是一个使用 Skywater Open PDK 130nm 技术实现的可数字合成的 SerDes（串行器/解串器）架构。SerDes 用于高速通信，将并行数据转换为串行数据传输，并通过接收端转换回并行数据。该项目使用 OpenLane 和 Virtuoso Cadence 工具，Verilog HDL 编码，映射到 Sky130 CMOS 技术。项目包括串行器、解串器、基于反相器的传输驱动、带有电阻反馈的反相器作为接收传感元件、DFF 用于数据采样、以及过采样 CDR 用于时钟和数据恢复等模块。相关文件如 gds、spice 和 netlist 文件已上传到相应文件夹。项目遵循 GPL-3.0 许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源芯片设计的挑战与进展

不同观点：
• [jauntywundrkind] 认为开源CPU设计虽然起步较容易，但要让芯片真正运行起来非常困难。他指出，许多设备使用相同的设计家族，如USB主机控制器、音频芯片、DRAM控制器和PCIe模块等，这些模块化设计已经被各种代工厂验证。尽管一个5年未更新的项目没有明确成果，但仅仅是尝试进行芯片设计已经是巨大的进步。开放源代码芯片的成熟需要不断尝试、调整和改进。

• [gchadwick] 关注芯片设计中的细节问题，尤其是模拟仿真难以捕捉的罕见事件。他认为，这些事件在实际硅片运行中可能会频繁发生，导致芯片无法正常工作。尽管如此，他对开源工具和工艺设计套件（PDK）能够支持这样的开源设计工作表示赞赏。

• [peter_d_sherman] 提供了一个相关的书籍资源，即《High-Speed Serial I/O Made Simple: A Designers’ Guide, with FPGA Applications》，为讨论增加了技术背景和学习资源。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于开源芯片设计的实际可行性和细节处理。一方面，jauntywundrkind强调开放源代码芯片设计的潜力和必要步骤；另一方面，gchadwick指出实际操作中的技术难题，特别是在模拟和硅验证之间的差距。
- 评论中还提到了开放源代码工具和PDK的重要性，认为这些工具是支持开源芯片设计尝试的基础设施。
- peter_d_sherman提供的资源为对该主题感兴趣的人提供了进一步学习的途径，增强了讨论的技术深度。

OpenSERDES
Serializer/Deserializer (
SerDes
) is the most important functional block used in high speed communication.
SerDes converts parallel data into a serial (one bit) stream of data that is transmitted over a high-speed connection, such as LVDS, to a receiver that converts the serial stream back to the original, parallel data.
A global CLOCK signal is present to sequence the serialization and deserialization of data from one block to another.
Technology:
Skywater OpenPDK 130nm
Tools Used:
OpenLane, Virtuoso Cadence
The
Serializer
and
Deserializer
blocks are coded in Verilog HDL and synthesized using Openlane tool mapped to Sky130 CMOS technology. Simulation results and associated gds, spice and netlist files are uploaded in Serializer and Deserializer folders respectively
A chain of CMOS inverters is used as TX driver to drive the input capacitance of the channel. The gds, spice, netlist and. oa files for the same are present in
Inverter_Based_Tx
folder
A fully synthesizable Rx is designed using Resistive FB inverter followed by CMOS inverter as sensing and gain element respectively. The following DFF is used to sample the data using the clock recovered by the CDR.
Resistive Feedback inverter
is used as sensing element to sense low amplitude received signal at the front end of the receiver. Details of the implementation of Resistive FB inverter can be found in Resistive_FB_inverter folder
DFF is the simplest memory block to sample and store the data before deserializing. Master Slave DFF is implemented using NAND logic gates. Details of the same are present in
DFF
and
NAND
folders
Oversampling CDR
is used to recover the data and clock from the received signal. The CDR uses the data transitions to tune the clock frequency for proper decoding of received signal. The
Oversampling_CDR
folder contains the gds, spice and synthesized Verilog files generated from Openlane tool.

44306462.article_summary: OpenSERDES 是一个使用 Skywater Open PDK 130nm 技术实现的可数字合成的 SerDes（串行器/解串器）架构。SerDes 用于高速通信，将并行数据转换为串行数据传输，并通过接收端转换回并行数据。该项目使用 OpenLane 和 Virtuoso Cadence 工具，Verilog HDL 编码，映射到 Sky130 CMOS 技术。项目包括串行器、解串器、基于反相器的传输驱动、带有电阻反馈的反相器作为接收传感元件、DFF 用于数据采样、以及过采样 CDR 用于时钟和数据恢复等模块。相关文件如 gds、spice 和 netlist 文件已上传到相应文件夹。项目遵循 GPL-3.0 许可。

• [gchadwick] 关注芯片设计中的细节问题，尤其是模拟仿真难以捕捉的罕见事件。他认为，这些事件在实际硅片运行中可能会频繁发生，导致芯片无法正常工作。尽管如此，他对开源工具和工艺设计套件（PDK）能够支持这样的开源设计工作表示赞赏。

- peter_d_sherman提供的资源为对该主题感兴趣的人提供了进一步学习的途径，增强了讨论的技术深度。

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了大语言模型（LLM）是否会终结计算机编程这一争论，指出当前讨论缺乏细致分析。作者通过Google翻译的技术演变，特别是2016年后的神经机器翻译，来类比分析这一问题。尽管有人声称机器翻译将取代人工翻译和口译，但实际上这些职业的需求在增加。机器翻译虽有用，但无法处理上下文、文化敏感性和歧义，而这些正是翻译和口译工作的核心。例如，Google翻译在处理如挪威语等语言时，会直接翻译出不符合英语礼貌习惯的句子，而在复杂情况下（如法庭翻译），这种错误是不可接受的。因此，尽管机器翻译技术优秀，但它无法完全替代人工翻译，类似地，LLM也不会终结编程行业，而是改变其工作方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI翻译技术（尤其是大语言模型LLM）是否会取代人类翻译员，以及AI在各行业中的影响。

不同观点：
• [tkgally] 认为LLM在提供足够上下文的情况下，已经能够很好地完成翻译工作，尤其是在日英翻译中表现突出。LLM通过多轮修订和优化，能够生成与顶级专业翻译相媲美的结果，因此人类在纯粹翻译工作上的竞争力正在下降。
• [yoden] 持相对保守的观点，认为尽管AI是很好的工具，但它不会完全取代专业人士。以放射学为例，AI的效率提升并未减少对专业人员的需求，因此没必要过度担心AI取代人类翻译员。
• [philsnow] 强调翻译中的文化背景和本地化工作，认为AI可能无法理解和处理这些复杂的文化因素，举例说明了翻译中的文化调整（如皮克斯电影的本地化）。
• [sodality2] 指出文章未提及的一个观点：那些使用AI创建应用程序的人可能以前从未雇佣过软件工程师，因此AI的影响可能不像预期的那么大。然而，在软件开发领域，AI的影响可能更显著，因为低成本的软件开发机会可能导致对专业工程师需求的减少。
• [NicuCalcea] 通过轶事和论坛讨论，表明翻译员的工作机会确实在减少，尤其是在LLM引入后，许多翻译员对AI持悲观态度。
• [jezzamon] 强调了对翻译结果的信任问题，认为人们更容易信任人类翻译而不是机器翻译，因为无法自行验证机器翻译的正确性，仍需要专家的介入。
• [neilv] 补充了翻译员处理习语、文化参考、文化价值观、配音演员匹配和艺术散文等方面的专业工作，认为这些是LLM目前难以胜任的。
• [krackers] 认为Google Translate不如DeepL，甚至不如LLM，指出Google Translate在速度和准确性上的不足。
• [devnullbrain] 批评Google Translate的表现，指出其在语言检测和错误纠正上的问题，认为现代软件过于自信，不容用户纠正错误。
• [darvinyraghpath] 认为尽管LLM不能真正取代工程师，但AI已成为行业内打压工程师的工具，导致软件行业工作质量下降，且这种趋势可能继续。

补充讨论：
• [ryao] 提到翻译中的语气问题，认为在不同英语变体中，"I will have the potatoes" 是否傲慢存在文化差异。
• [dr_dshiv] 对未来翻译员数量增加持乐观态度，认为尽管LLM有语气问题，但通过良好的提示可以解决。

争议焦点：
• AI是否能完全取代人类翻译员，特别是在处理文化背景、语气和专业术语方面的能力。
• AI对软件开发行业的影响，是否会导致对专业工程师需求的减少。
• 现代翻译工具（如Google Translate）的准确性和可靠性问题。

44302870.article_content:
What Google Translate Can Tell Us About Vibecoding | Ingrid's Space
What Google Translate Can Tell Us About Vibecoding
Jun 17, 2025
6 minute read
There has been rather a lot of doomsaying (and perhaps astroturfing) lately about LLMs as the end of computer programming. Much of the discussion has been lacking nuance, so I’d like to add mine. I see claims from one side that “I used
$LLM_SERVICE_PROVIDER
to make a small throwaway tool, so all programmers will be unemployed in
$ARBITRARY_TIME_WINDOW
”, and from the other side flat-out rejections of the idea that this type of tool can have any utility.
1
I think it best sheds light on these claims to examine them in the context of another field that’s been ahead of the curve on this: translation.
Google translate has been around for a while, and has gone through some technological iterations; I’m most interested in discussing its recent incarnations since the switch to
neural machine translation
in 2016. Over the years I’ve heard much made about how this is the end of translation and interpretation as professions. I suspect the people who say such things have never actually worked with translator or interpreter. The emblematic example I’ve encountered is “I went on holiday to Japan and we used Google Translate everywhere, there’s no need to hire an interpreter or learn Japanese anymore”. While this undoubtedly speaks for the usefulness of current machine translation technology, the second half of the sentence calls for some scrutiny, particularly “anymore”. I feel confident in asserting that people who say this would not have hired a translator or learned Japanese in a world without Google Translate; they’d have either not gone to Japan at all, or gone anyway and been clueless foreigners as tourists are wont to do.
Indeed it turns out
the number of available job opportunities for translators and interpreters has actually been increasing
. This is not to say that the technology isn’t good, I think it’s pretty close to as good as it can be at what it does. It’s also not to say that machine translation hasn’t changed the profession of translation: in the article linked above, Bridget Hylak, a representative from the American Translators Association, is quoted as saying “Since the advent of neural machine translation (NMT) around 2016, which marked a significant improvement over traditional machine translation like Google Translate, we [translators and interpreters] have been integrating AI into our workflows.”
To explain this apparent contradiction, we need to understand what it is translators actually do because, like us programmers, they suffer from having the nature of their work consistently misunderstood by non-translators. The laity’s image of a translator is a walking dictionary and grammar reference, who substitutes words and and grammatical structures from one language to another with ease, the reality is that a translators’ and interpreters’ work is mostly about ensuring context, navigating ambiguity, and handling cultural sensitivity. This is what Google Translate cannot currently do.
To give a simple example, Norwegian is an extremely closely related language to English and should be an easy translation candidate. The languages share a tonne of cognates, very similar grammar, and similar cultural context; even the idioms tend to translate verbatim. Yet there remain important cultural differences, and a particularly friction-prone one is Norwegian’s lack of polite language. It’s technically possible to say please in Norwegian (vÃ¦r sÃ¥ snill, or vennligst), but Norwegians tend to prefer blunt communication, and these are not used much in practice. At the dinner table a Norwegian is likely to say something like “Jeg vil ha potetene” (literally “I will have the potatoes”, which sounds presumptuous and haughty in English) where a brit might say “Could I please have some potatoes?”. A good interpreter would have the necessary context for this (or ask for clarification if they’re not sure) and provide a sensitive translation, Google Translate just gives the blunt direct translation. You can probably work past such misunderstandings at dinner with your foreign in-laws (and people do), but it should be apparent why it’s inadvisable to
subsititute Google Translate for an interpreter at a court hearing
. And Norwegian is an easy case. Returning to our tourists, Japanese has wildly different grammar to English, including things like omitting subjects from sentences where it’s apparent from context. In many of these cases you can’t construct a grammatical English sentence without a subject, so Google translate will make one up. Would you be comfortable with a computer inserting a made up subject into your sentence?
All this is not to say Google Translate is doing a bad job. Were I given “Jeg vil ha potetene” with no context or ability to clarify and asked to translate it to English, I’d give the same answer. Maybe the person does want to be rude, how should I know?

data.title: Zed Debugger
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary: Zed编辑器终于推出了原生的多语言调试功能，支持零设置、快速启动，并提供灵活的调试体验。调试器采用Debug Adapter Protocol（DAP），确保多语言一致性，并可通过扩展自定义。功能包括代码断点、会话控制、模块化面板、多会话支持、远程调试等。社区对该功能期待已久，其推出解决了用户迁移到Zed的主要障碍，许多人表示这将使Zed成为VSCode的强有力替代品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zed编辑器的使用体验及其功能

不同观点：
• **Johntash** 认为Zed编辑器的性能出色，尤其是在通过SSH进行远程编辑时表现优异，并且比VSCode更少占用资源。他正在尝试将其作为日常驱动工具，直到遇到其难以处理的问题。

• **AbuAssar** 对Zed逐步演变为一个功能齐全的轻量级IDE感到兴奋。他认为Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) 和 Language Server Protocol (LSP) 是过去十年中编程工具领域的最佳发展，暗示这些功能对Zed的进步起到了重要作用。

• **Vrajspandya1** 以前因为Zed缺乏行内调试功能而没有使用它，但在Zed加入调试功能后，他表示愿意再次尝试使用。

补充讨论：
• 用户对Zed的性能和资源占用情况有积极评价，特别是在与VSCode对比时。
• Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) 和 Language Server Protocol (LSP) 被认为是提升编程工具体验的重要功能，受到一些用户的推崇。
• 行内调试功能的缺失曾是用户不选择Zed的原因之一，但随着该功能的加入，一些用户表示愿意重新尝试Zed。
• 争议的焦点可能在于Zed的功能完善程度及其能否在各种开发需求下替代其他成熟IDE（如VSCode）。

data.title: Now might be the best time to learn software development
data.author: nathanfig
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具对开发者及软件行业的影响

不同观点：
• **AI工具提供心理支持，推动工作进展**：guicen认为AI工具不仅提供实际帮助，还能在心理上给予支持，减少孤独感，特别是在工作卡壳时提供推动力。
• **对AI过度炒作的担忧**：psunavy03通过讽刺COBOL的历史，暗示当前对AI工具的炒作可能言过其实。michaelteter同样认为AI是被过度炒作的“银弹”，并预期其效果可能不如宣传的那样显著，但同时也承认这对有创造力的开发者来说是一个机会。
• **AI对就业市场的双重影响**：nathanfig提出了一种反叙事，认为尽管AI可能威胁到开发者的工作，但也有机会创造新的收入来源。temporallobe和prisenco则指出，非技术人员使用低代码/无代码工具往往会造成混乱，最终仍需技术人员来清理。
• **AI对开发者技能的需求转变**：abalashov和bentt认为，AI工具的出现将使开发者的价值从单纯编码能力转向领域专业知识和问题解决能力。bentt进一步指出，AI热潮促使公司追逐投资者青睐，但这并不一定意味着AI工具的实际效用。
• **AI工具在教育和学习中的作用**：NoPicklez和Leo-thorne强调AI工具在学习和理解编程概念方面的优势，认为AI可以帮助新手更容易上手，但最终掌握技能仍需个人努力。
• **AI工具的局限性和未来发展**：dehrmann和eqvinox对AI工具的长期影响持怀疑态度，讨论了需求弹性和AI能力的上限。KurSix总结道，尽管AI工具非常强大，但它们尚不能替代深度理解和批判性思维。

补充讨论：
• **开发者工作价值的反思**：rossdavidh提出，21世纪的开发者大部分时间都花在获取注意力上，而非创造真正有用的东西，这引发了对开发者工作价值的深思。
• **学习计算机科学的重要性**：clpmsf认为，当前是学习计算机科学的好时机，而非仅仅是软件开发，强调了基础知识和理论的重要性。

争议焦点：
• **AI工具是否会取代开发者**：一部分人认为AI工具降低了编程门槛，但最终仍需人类开发者的深度理解和实际操作；另一部分人则担心AI会导致开发者失业或降低其价值。
• **AI工具的实际效用与炒作**：对AI工具的实际效用存在不同看法，一些人认为其被过度炒作，而另一些人则看到其在教育和生产力提升方面的潜力。

data.author: perihelions
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某宣言的公开性质及其时机的争议，以及科学和科学资金的政治化问题

不同观点：
• StatsAreFun认为宣言的公开性质和引发的媒体关注有政治操作的嫌疑。他质疑为何不直接与NIH领导层接触以寻求解决方案，并指出此前NIH及其资助机构的问题早已存在，"为什么现在才提出来"成为一个关键问题。他还提到了去年涉及Dr. Eliezer Masliah的研究丑闻。

• jekwoooooe强调了此宣言的时机问题，认为在之前行政当局禁止某些研究时没有类似的宣言，特别是在涉及跨性别医学的问题上。他批评美国医学协会（AMA）忽视英国关于儿童激素治疗无益甚至有害的发现，质疑为何当时没有类似的抗议。

• freen则认为任何对现任行政当局的批评都不可能持久存在，暗示存在审查或压制批评言论的情况。

• TrnsltLife指出科学和科学资金的政治化并非仅在现任行政当局存在，而是在上一任行政当局也同样存在，只是当时科学家的世界观与政府更一致。他提到那些与主流科学家世界观不一致的科学家曾遭到压制和 silenced。

补充讨论：
• 宣言的时机和动机受到质疑，尤其是为什么选择现在发布，而不是在之前出现类似问题的时候。
• 科学政治化的历史背景和不同行政当局下的表现成为讨论的重要方面，有观点认为这种政治化在不同政府任期内都有，只是表现形式不同。
• 评论中还涉及了对具体事件（如Dr. Eliezer Masliah的研究丑闻）和政策（如跨性别医学研究）的批评。

争议焦点：宣言的公开性质与时机、科学政治化的历史与现状、以及对现任或前任行政当局处理科学问题的批评是否合理。

data.title: The Great Decoupling (Or Why Your Clicks Are Down and Impressions Up)
data.author: duck
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在Google搜索结果中出现的“零点击SEO”现象及其对网站流量的影响。随着AI Overviews的推出，某些关键词的搜索结果会出现两次曝光机会，一个在传统蓝色链接中，另一个在AI Overview中。这导致印象（impressions）增加，但点击（clicks）减少，因为用户无需点击即可获得所需信息。这种“大脱钩”现象使得印象和点击不再相关联，印象飙升而点击骤降。文章建议使用Ahrefs的工具来分析AI Overviews对关键词排名的影响，并监测可能因此趋势受到影响的关键词。这一趋势可能持续，直到AI Overviews全面推出并成为默认搜索体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google搜索结果页提供足够信息的影响以及第三方工具（如ahrefs）的访问权限问题

不同观点：
• jaoane认为Google在过去十年中最出色的改进是让用户无需离开搜索结果页就能获取所需信息。这一观点强调了Google搜索体验的提升，使用户能够更快速、高效地解决问题。

• LordShredda则关注第三方工具（如ahrefs）的访问问题，指出ahrefs没有始终遵守robots.txt规则，并建议其他用户也阻止其访问自己的webserver。这一观点反映了对数据抓取和隐私保护的关注，强调了对不遵守规则的工具采取防御措施的必要性。

补充讨论：
• jaoane的观点隐含了对搜索引擎优化的认可，认为Google通过整合信息提高了用户体验，但也可能对依赖流量的网站产生影响。

• LordShredda的建议涉及到技术性和隐私性问题，尤其是对robots.txt这一标准的遵守，反映出对网络爬虫和数据收集行为的警惕。

争议焦点：
• Google搜索结果页提供完整信息对内容提供者（如网站站长）和用户之间的利益平衡问题。
• 第三方工具（如ahrefs）访问和抓取数据时的合规性和隐私保护问题。

Ryan Law
Ryan Law is the Director of Content Marketing at Ahrefs. Ryan has 13 years experience as a writer, content strategist, team lead, marketing director, VP, CMO, and agency founder. He's helped dozens of companies improve their content marketing and SEO, including Google, Zapier, GoDaddy, Clearbit, and Algolia. He's also a novelist and the creator of two content marketing courses.
